subject: geography
title: TNCs and Global Production Networks
welcome_lead: Follow an iPhone's journey across continents to understand transnational corporations.
meta_desc: Geography HL Adventure: transnational corporations, global production networks and glocalisation.
final_note: You have followed the supply chain. Power and value flow unevenly across these networks.

concepts.def: Firm operating in multiple countries through foreign direct investment and global supply chains.
Geographically distributed system of value creation incorporating firms, suppliers and institutions.
Cross-border investment giving lasting control or influence over an enterprise.
Contracting out parts of production to independent suppliers.
Relocating production processes to another country, often within the same corporation.
Adaptation of global products to local tastes and regulations, e.g. McDonald's menu variation.

walkthroughs.body_html: TNCs like Apple, Toyota, Unilever and Samsung coordinate networks of subsidiaries, contractors and logistics. UNCTAD estimates around 60,000 TNCs with 500,000 affiliates account for around two-thirds of world trade. Inward FDI tends to concentrate in HICs and selected MICs.

'Smile curve' analyses show that value concentrates in R&D, branding and post-sale services rather than manufacturing. China's role evolved from assembly to higher-value design; Vietnam, Bangladesh and Ethiopia are absorbing labour-intensive activities formerly in coastal China.

Glocalisation is central to TNC strategy: KFC offers congee in China; McDonald's offers paneer wraps in India. Standardised global brands meet localised marketing, distribution and product design — a useful nuance against the 'McDonaldisation' thesis.

mcqs.q: What does Spearman's rank correlation coefficient measure?
options: The strength and direction of a relationship between two ranked variables. Values range from -1 (perfect negative) through 0 (no correlation) to +1 (perfect positive).
Ocean acidification is caused by acid rain falling on the sea.
Spearman's rank measures the average rank of all the data points.
A Spearman value close to 1 proves that one variable causes the other.

mcqs.q: What weather does an anticyclone (high pressure system) bring?
options: High pressure brings stormy weather because the air pushes down hard.
Spearman's rank measures the average rank of all the data points.
Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.
Descending air warms and dries, suppressing cloud formation — so anticyclones bring clear, settled weather: hot in summer, cold and frosty in winter.

mcqs.q: Why is ocean acidification a separate threat from ocean warming?
options: Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.
Ocean acidification is just another name for ocean warming.
Acidification occurs because oceans absorb atmospheric CO2, forming carbonic acid and lowering pH — this dissolves calcium carbonate shells and corals, independent of any warming.
Ocean acidification is caused by acid rain falling on the sea.
